Two self-contained UX features for the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon. Build our own; do not copy any competitor's code, copy, or branding.

YOUR FILES (owned exclusively): components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx (+ any small helper you add under components/customer/mail/), components/ChatWidget.tsx, and whatever server piece the chat typing indicator needs (read how ChatWidget talks to the backend first — likely an action in lib/actions-chat*.ts or an app/api/chat route; you may edit the chat send/poll path ONLY as needed for the typing indicator, and say so). Plus any new test files. Do NOT touch mail SENDING logic (lib/actions-mail.ts, lib/mailer.ts) beyond what's needed to carry a richer body — read them to understand the send path but keep changes minimal and additive.

FEATURE 1 — Rich-text mail compose. The compose popup currently sends plain text. Give it a real formatting toolbar like a normal mail app:
- Bold, italic, underline, font size, and (if it fits the design cleanly) text colour and lists.
- PASTE IMAGES into the body — inline images, either as data: URIs or uploaded and referenced (check whether the mail send path / Mailcow supports HTML with inline/attached images; wire to whatever it supports, and if inline images can't be delivered, fall back to attaching them and say so rather than silently dropping them).
- Copy-paste of formatted content should be preserved reasonably.
- The composed HTML must be SANITISED before it is sent (this platform sends real mail; never ship an XSS vector or a malformed body). Read how existing mail HTML is handled (lib/mail/render.ts has a safeHtml) and reuse it.
- The send action must carry the HTML body end-to-end so what the customer composed is what the recipient gets. Verify the send path actually transmits the HTML — do not add a toolbar that formats a body the send then flattens to plain text (this codebase's cardinal rule: never ship a control whose outcome isn't verified).

FEATURE 2 — Live-chat "typing…" indicator. The customer support live chat (ChatWidget.tsx + admin inbox) should show an animated "typing…" indicator when the other party is composing.
- Add the animated indicator UI (three-dot pulse or similar, matching the Nxeon theme).
- Wire the signal: when one side is typing, the other sees it. The chat likely polls or uses SSE — read the existing transport and add a lightweight "typing" flag (a timestamped field the poll returns, or a transient signal). Keep it cheap; a typing ping every couple seconds max, and it must expire on its own so a stuck flag doesn't show "typing" forever.
- If wiring a real bi-directional signal is too invasive for the current transport, implement the ANIMATION and the local "I am typing" send, and clearly report what the receiving side needs to display it — do not fake a received-typing state that isn't really wired.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Match the Nxeon design system exactly — read neighbouring components, reuse tokens/spacing.
- Controlled inputs where the customer types (React 19 resets uncontrolled fields on form-action submit — this has caused real data loss here).

VERIFY: `npx tsc --noEmit` = 0; `npm test` stays green (582) and grows; add tests for pure logic (HTML sanitisation of the composed body, the typing-flag expiry) and use stripCommentsAndStrings from test/_source-tools.ts for any source tripwire. Do NOT build in /opt/nxeon/.next. Do NOT run standalone scripts from a symlinked-node_modules tree (production creds hazard). Do not deploy, restart, or commit — I integrate centrally. Never send real mail to a third party.

Report: what each feature does now, exactly how the HTML body and the typing signal travel end-to-end (verified, not assumed), what falls back and why, and tests added/proven.

So I need to check what Mailcow actually supports for inline versus attached images, and if inline images won't work, I should fall back to attaching them instead while letting the user know what happened. For the image approach, CID attachments are the cleanest solution since nodemailer already supports them — I'd reference images with `` and safeHtml allows the cid scheme. I'm weighing whether to use data URIs for inline images in the composed HTML—they'd display immediately in the composer and preserve what the user created, but safeHtml strips data: from src attributes as a security measure for inbound mail. The question is whether that same restriction applies to outbound mail the user is composing, where data URIs are actually safe since they're not untrusted content. The better approach is to use CID (Content-ID) references for inline images instead—when the user pastes an image, I'll insert an `` with a placeholder reference that gets resolved through a dedicated, safe handling path rather than relying on data URIs to survive sanitization. I need to update the SendAttachment type to include optional `cid` and `inline` fields, then modify the mail actions to pass these through to nodemailer so it builds the multipart/related structure correctly — this is the standard, universally-supported way to embed inline images. There's a consideration around how safeHtml processes the outbound HTML though. The Composer already runs safeHtml on signatures, but currently the user body is just escaped plaintext. With rich text support, I'll need to run safeHtml over the full composed HTML body. I'm checking that safeHtml preserves `cid:` URLs in image src attributes — it does, since cid doesn't match any of the blocked schemes like javascript or data. It also keeps inline style attributes intact, which is necessary for formatting like font-size and color that the toolbar produces. Now I'm weighing whether to implement CID inline images or take the safer approach of converting pasted images to regular attachments. CID support is more professional and genuinely deliverable, but it requires modifying the mail sending logic. The simpler fallback of attaching images instead keeps the implementation minimal and still satisfies the requirement not to silently drop images — the recipient just gets them as attachments rather than inline. I'm leaning toward implementing CID properly since it's the correct approach for email and I can make the server changes small and additive with clear comments. I'll create a pure helper function in a new module that extracts images from the HTML, converts them to CID references, sanitizes the HTML, and returns both the cleaned markup and a list of inline images with their metadata. ## What each feature does now

### Feature 1 — Rich-text mail compose (`components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx`)
The plain `<textarea>` is replaced by a formatting toolbar + a `contentEditable` editor:
- **Toolbar:** Bold, Italic, Underline, font-size select (Small/Normal/Large/Huge), text-colour picker, bulleted + numbered lists, and an insert-image button. Buttons `preventDefault` on mousedown so the selection survives the click.
- **Paste images inline:** pasting an image inserts it at the caret; the toolbar image button does the same via a file picker.
- **Formatted copy-paste preserved:** non-image pastes keep the browser's rich paste; everything is sanitised at send.
- **Controlled-input safety:** the editor is ref-driven (contentEditable can't be a React-controlled value), and its HTML is read from the ref only at submit — never mirrored into state — so there's no uncontrolled-reset data-loss path. The submit is an `onClick` handler, not a form action, so the React-19 form-action reset doesn't apply. All other fields (To/Cc/Subject) stay controlled as before.

### Feature 2 — Live-chat typing indicator (`components/ChatWidget.tsx`, `components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx`)
Fully bidirectional, animated three-dot pulse (Tailwind `animate-pulse` with staggered `animationDelay` — no new global keyframes, matches the brand `bg-brand-300`). Visitor sees "Support is typing"; agent sees "<name> is typing…".

## How the HTML body travels end-to-end (verified in code, not assumed)
1. `Composer.submit()` reads `editorRef.current.innerHTML`, then `prepareComposedBody()` (new `components/customer/mail/compose-html.ts`) **extracts base64 raster images → `cid:` references** and runs the result through **`safeHtml`** (the existing sanitiser in `lib/mail/render.ts`).
2. The sanitised body is wrapped in the light-background styled `<div>` and sent as `payload.html`; inline images go into `payload.attachments` each carrying a `cid`. Plain-text alternative = editor `innerText`.
3. `MailClient.handleSend` → `sendMessage(payload)` in `lib/actions-mail.ts`.
4. The send action **re-sanitises server-side** (`safeHtml(payload.html)` — last gate, never trusts the client), builds nodemailer attachments marking cid-bearing ones `contentDisposition: "inline"`, compiles the MIME once (`streamTransport`), and SMTP-sends the exact `raw` bytes (same bytes appended to Sent). So the composed HTML is what the recipient gets — the send does **not** flatten it to text.

**Inline images — what's delivered vs. fallback:** raster pastes (png/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp) are delivered **inline** via `cid:` in multipart/related (universally rendered). `safeHtml` deliberately neutralises all `data:` URLs, which is exactly why images are lifted to `cid:` *before* sanitisation rather than shipped as `data:` — a raw data-image would otherwise be blanked to `src="#"`. **SVG and non-raster/`data:text/html` images are intentionally dropped** (not delivered) because inline SVG is an XSS surface; this is deliberate, tested, and noted here rather than silent.

## How the typing signal travels (verified)
Transient, in-memory, self-expiring store `lib/chat-typing.ts` (module-level Map, `TYPING_TTL_MS = 6000`, same pattern as `lib/rate-limit.ts`) — no DB writes, no migration.
- **Visitor → agent:** widget POSTs `/api/chat/typing` (new route, its own rate-limit so it never eats the message-send budget) throttled to ~1/2.5s while typing → `markTyping(convId,"visitor")`. `listConversations`/`getConversation` return `visitorTyping: readTyping(id).visitor`; admin inbox renders the indicator.
- **Agent → visitor:** admin inbox calls the new `signalAgentTyping` server action (gated by `requireArea("support")`, throttled ~1/2.5s) → `markTyping(convId,"agent")`. The existing `GET /api/chat` poll now returns `typing.agent`; the widget shows the indicator.
- **Expiry:** a flag ages out after 6s and the poll can only *clear* a stale one, so a crashed tab can never leave "typing…" stuck.
